Testing strategy and quality gates\n\n### 14.1 Tiers\n\n| Tier | What | Runs |\n|---|---|---|\n| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. No flags, frame-exact, deterministic | Every commit |\n| **T-degradation** | Synthetic blur / rotation / keystone / glare / rolling-shutter tearing applied to rendered frames. **Assert decode *rates*, not booleans** | Nightly |\n| **T-real-capture** | Frames → Y4M → Chromium fake camera. Proven in research (byte-exact, including late-join at 700 ms) | Nightly |\n| **T-scale** | Synthetic 4 GB stream at the block layer; assert flat memory across 21,800 blocks | Nightly |\n| **T-long-run** | **20–30 minute sustained run** on real devices to validate thermal behavior (R11), duty-cycle economics (D27), and sustained throughput. Tracks fps decline, decode rate, and effective goodput over time. **This is the ONLY tier that can measure R11 and D27** — the 60 s floor in §13.2 structurally excludes thermal phenomena. | Weekly (or per thermal-related change) |\n| **T-physical-rig** | Two real devices, fixed mounting, the §13.2 denominator. **This is the acceptance gate for §13.1 throughput** — nothing else can measure it | Per release |\n| **T-manual-iOS** | Full pass on a real iPhone. **Not CI-testable at any price** — WebKit cannot fake a camera, the Simulator has none | Per release |\n\n> **Trap, already paid for:** `--use-fake-device-for-media-capture` **does not exist**. It\n> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n\n### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n\n**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\nrejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\nround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. An ASCII suite marks every library safe,\nincluding the broken ones. The nastiest case, `@zxing/library.getText()`, returns the\n**correct length** while collapsing bytes ≥ 0x80 to U+FFFD — a length assertion passes and\nthe file is silently ruined. Assert on bytes, at multiple lengths, over 0x00–0xFF.\n\n### 14.3 Conformance vectors\n\nShip as fixtures, because they are what a third-party implementation would need:\n\n- `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` — bit-exact, pinning the PRNG (I3)\n- Header encode/decode round-trip at every field boundary\n- Beacon encode/decode including absent optional fields\n- Repair-code round-trip, including a deliberately mistyped code\n- A **two-realm test**: the same built app in two contexts, one sending, one receiving —\n  the only test that actually verifies the \"both roles, one page\" constraint\n\n### 14.4 The no-network assertion\n\nCI MUST fail the build if the running app issues **any** network request after load —\nincluding the lazy WASM fetch described in §6.5, which is the most likely violation and\ndoes not occur until the first decode, so **the assertion must exercise a decode**\n(intercept `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/`Image`; fail on any call). This is the\nexecutable form of T7 and of concept.md constraint 1.\n\n### 14.5 Quality gates\n\n| Gate | Requirement |\n|---|---|\n| **G1** | Typecheck, lint, unit, property, stub-camera all green |\n| **G2** | No network requests (§14.4) |\n| **G3** | Bundle-size budget not exceeded; dependencies pinned to exact versions, no post-install scripts (T5) |\n| **G4** | Simulation assertions for D5/D6/D25 pass (I2), **at the adopted K** |\n| **G5** | Memory budget (I6a) holds on T-scale. **Runs nightly**, so it gates the nightly build, not each commit — see the cadence note below |\n| **G6** | Throughput budgets (§13.1) hold on T-physical-rig — release only |\n| **G7** | `python3 docs/research/sim/ge_cost_model.py --check` passes — **the plan's §3.1/§4 numbers match what the model computes**. A UTF-8 string can use up to 4 bytes per codepoint. */\n  MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS: 32, // 32 × 4 = 128, guarantees never exceeds MAX_FILENAME_BYTES\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 codepoint count for MIME type (T2). */\n  MAX_MIMETYPE_CODEPOINTS: 14, // 14 × 4 = 56, fits within MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES\n} as const;\n\n/**\n * Calculate K_manifest from blockCount and blockHashLen.\n *\n * K_manifest is the number of blocks needed to store the block hash manifest.\n * The manifest contains blockCount × blockHashLen bytes (all block hashes),\n * divided into blocks of size BLOCK (196608 bytes = K × L).\n *\n * Formula: K_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)\n *\n * @param blockCount - Number of data blocks (from beacon)\n * @param blockHashLen - Length of each block hash in bytes (from beacon)\n * @returns Number of blocks needed to store the manifest\n */\nfunction calculateKManifest(blockCount: number, blockHashLen: number): number {\n  const BLOCK = 196608; // K × L where K=768, L=256 (from core/params.ts)\n  const manifestBytes = blockCount * blockHashLen;\n  return Math.ceil(manifestBytes / BLOCK);\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a beacon from bytes.\n *\n * Beacon format: [body fields...][crc32(4)]\n * The CRC-32 covers all beacon body fields and MUST be validated before\n * any metadata (including streamId) is trusted.\n *\n * **Validation order is critical:**\n * 1. (bytes[offset] << 24) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1] << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 2] << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 3];\n    offset += 4;\n    return value >>> 0; // Force unsigned\n  };\n\n  const readU24 = () => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset] << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1] << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 2];\n    offset += 3;\n bytes[offset++];\n\n  const readBytes = (n: number) => {\n    const value = bytes.subarray(offset, offset + n);\n    offset += n;\n    return value;\n  };\n\n  const readString = (maxLen: number) => {\n    const len = readU8();\n    if (len > maxLen) {\n      throw new BeaconValidationError(\n        'E-META-BOUNDS',\n        `String length ${len} exceeds maximum ${maxLen}`,\n        {length: len, max: maxLen}\n      );\n    }\n    const strBytes = readBytes(len);\n    // Decode as UTF-8\n    const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true});\n    try {\n      return expected ${expectedSize} (body+CRC)`,\n      {actual: bytes.length, expected: expectedSize}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Read the CRC-32 from the last 4 bytes\n  const storedCrc = (bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n The manifest hash detects this\n * corruption immediately and forces re-decode of the manifest.\n *\n * Reference: plan.md §7.2, §7.6, §12 (T1)\n */\n\nimport {crc32} from '../frame/crc.js';\n\n/**\n * Compute the SHA-256 hash of a block and truncate it.\n *\n * Per plan.md §7.6, block hashes are SHA-256 truncated to blockHashLen bytes\n * (default 4 bytes). This provides a per-block false accept rate of 2^-32 (~5×10^-6),\n * which across 21,845 blocks (4 GB file) yields ~0.01 expected collisions — comfortably\n * below the whole-file hash's job.\n *\n * **Performance note:** This uses crypto.subtle.digest which is async. For a 192 KB\n * block at 768 fragments, this is called once per block on the sender and once per\n * verified block on the receiver.\n *\n * @param block - Block data (K × L bytes, typically 192 KB)\n * @param blockHashLen - Truncation length (from beacon, typically 4 bytes)\n * @returns Promise resolving to truncated hash bytes\n * @throws {Error} If blockHashLen is invalid or Web Crypto API fails\n */\nexport async function computeBlockHash(block: Uint8Array, blockHashLen: number): Promise<Uint8Array> {\n  if (blockHashLen < 1 || blockHashLen > 32) {\n    throw new Error(\n      `Invalid blockHashLen: ${blockHashLen} (must be 1-32 bytes for SHA-256 truncation)`\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Compute full SHA-256 hash\n  const fullHash = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', block);\n\n  // Truncate to blockHashLen bytes\n  return new Uint8Array(fullHash).slice(0, blockHashLen);\n}\n\n/**\n * Compute the manifest hash (CRC-32) for beacon transmission.\n *\n * The manifest is `blockCount × blockHashLen` bytes containing all block hashes\n * in block order. This function computes its CRC-32 for the beacon's manifestHash\n * field (§7.2), enabling receivers to validate manifest integrity.\n *\n * **Critical:** This CRC-32 is the ONLY integrity check for the manifest data.\n * A corrupted manifest would cause hundreds of blocks to fail verification\n * forever (infinite E12 retry loop). The manifest hash prevents this livelock.\n *\n * @param manifest - Block hash manifest data (blockCount × blockHashLen bytes)\n * @returns CRC-32 checksum (4 bytes as big-endian number)\n */\nexport function computeManifestHash(manifest: Uint8Array): number {\n  return crc32(manifest);\n}\n\n/**\n * Validate a decoded manifest against the beacon's hash.\n *\n * After fountain-decoding the manifest (§7.6), the receiver MUST compute its CRC-32\n * and compare against the beacon's manifestHash field. The\n * per-packet fcrc (CRC-8) is a routing guard, not integrity. QR's Reed-Solomon\n * makes undetected corruption rare but not impossible.
